newsitem.title: CANADA: Striking Canada workers reject Safeway deal.
newsitem.headline: Striking Canada workers reject Safeway deal.

text.p: Striking Canada Safeway Ltd. workers in Alberta's two biggest cities have rejected what the company called its final labour contract offer.

In Calgary, the United Food and Commercial Workers union said 60.4 percent of the more than 1,500 employees who voted late Tuesday rejected the offer, which was presented by the grocery chain on March 24.

The move followed an 80 percent rejection of the proposal by Edmonton Safeway employees on Monday. Canada Safeway employees in other Alberta cities and towns were slated to vote on the offer on Wednesday.

Unionized workers at Alberta's 73 Canada Safeway stores in Alberta walked off the job last Tuesday, after the company, a unit of Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway Inc., presented a final offer and broke off bargaining talks.
The union has been without a contract since March 1996.

Doug O'Halloran, president of the union's Calgary local, told the Calgary Herald newspaper the union would likely send a letter to Canada Safeway on Thursday to request a return to the bargaining table.
Canada Safeway, however, said it had no plans to resume talks.

The company's contract offer included a 50-cent-per-hour wage increase and a C$1,000 payment ($722) for full-time workers if the deal was ratified. The five-year contract would also give full-time and senior part-time employees pay hikes of 30 cents an hour in 1998 and 40 cents in 2000.
However, the union had demanded that the company fully restore C$2-an-hour wage rollbacks employees took in 1993.
Canada Safeway, Alberta's largest grocery chain with 10,000 employees, has operated during the first week of the strike using management and replacement workers.
